disease_label_per_paper: Anti-NMDAR encephalitis with imaging-invisible ovarian teratoma
presentation_summary: 25-year-old previously well white woman presented with two generalized tonic-clonic seizures after two weeks of prodromal flu-like symptoms and nonspecific headache.
She was agitated in the emergency department and required midazolam.
Routine blood tests were unremarkable; CT brain showed mild generalized cerebral edema.
Brain MRI showed bilateral temporal lobe lesions involving hippocampi and amygdalae, more extensive on the right, consistent with limbic encephalitis.
EEG showed periodic lateralized epileptiform discharges and slow-wave changes maximal in frontal and temporal regions.
She was initially treated for possible HSV encephalitis, but deteriorated with behavioral changes, memory impairment, hypoventilation, and coma requiring ICU airway support.
CSF showed elevated lymphocytes; CSF and serum anti-NMDAR antibodies were strongly positive.
Repeated pelvic MRI and whole-body PET did not show teratoma, but bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy on day 29 found a microscopic mature cystic teratoma with neural/glial elements.
After immunotherapy and tumor removal she improved, became seizure-free, and had only mild short-term memory impairment before later independent recovery.
